name: Superlative Density
description: Analyzes the frequency and contextual usage of superlative adjectives and adverbs (e.g., 'greatest', 'most significant', 'best', 'highest'). Large Language Models, particularly when instructed to be persuasive, authoritative, or comprehensive, tend to drastically overuse superlatives. This 'hyperbolic default' is a byproduct of their RLHF training to provide the 'most helpful' possible answer, often resulting in exaggerated, universally conclusive language. Human writers use superlatives sparingly, reserving them for genuine extremes, and instead rely on nuanced comparatives or specific descriptive evidence.
mechanism: The algorithm uses Part-of-Speech (POS) tagging to identify all superlative forms (JJS, RBS tags) within the text. It computes the density of these tokens relative to the total word count and total adjective/adverb count. If the text exhibits an abnormally high concentration of superlatives—especially in contexts that are supposed to be objective, such as informational articles or neutral analyses—it is strongly flagged as AI-generated marketing fluff or algorithmic summarization.
useCase: Highly effective for auditing product reviews, marketing copy, essays, and cover letters, where AI models instinctively default to an overly enthusiastic, hyperbolic tone.
strengths:
• Exceptional at detecting 'sales pitch' AI text and aggressively helpful algorithmic summaries.
• Very difficult to bypass using simple paraphrasing tools, as the underlying intent to maximize impact usually preserves the superlative structure.
limitations:
• May produce false positives on authentic human marketing copy, political speeches, or genuinely enthusiastic personal reviews where hyperbole is expected.
• Less effective on highly technical or scientific texts where AI is explicitly prompted to be strictly factual and neutral.
parameters:
Analysis: POS Tagging (Superlative Form Identification)
Metric: Superlative to Total Adjective/Word Ratio
Output: 0-100 Hyperbolic Language (Algorithmic Enthusiasm) Score
accuracy: Moderate to High — 72-80% accuracy. A strong lexical indicator that works best when interpreted alongside emotional tone and vocabulary variance metrics.

references.title: Bhattacharjee, A. et al. (2020). Investigating the Role of Emotion in AI-Generated Text. ACL.
Guo, B. et al. (2023). How Close is ChatGPT to Human Experts? Comparison Corpus, Evaluation, and Detection. arXiv.
